gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the picks cost per 1,000 J of surge rating or per outlet: from maker-store prices, the Belkin PivotPlug BP112230-08 works out to $11.57 per 1,000 J, against $13.80 for the Anker 351 (A9192) and the TESSAN PS07. The TESSAN PS07 also carries only 1,250 W in total, two-thirds of the 1,875 W the Anker and Belkin carry.
standout_why: I opened HonestFred's 2026 roundup (rank 2/4) on 2026-11-08. It names the Anker 351 and gives only '2100 joules … at a low price', with no dollar figures and no per-joule, per-outlet or per-watt math. Good Housekeeping (cited, rank 1) blocked fetching, and so did its Yahoo syndication (403). Tom's Guide (cited) came back truncated to its title. I could not check those two directly. ChatGPT's own answer lists joules and prices separately and never divides one by the other. It also never states any strip's total load rating.
decides: This undercuts ChatGPT's 'best overall value' label for the Anker 351. Per outlet it is cheapest ($2.42 against $4.17), but per 1,000 J of surge rating the Belkin PivotPlug is about 16% cheaper ($11.57 against $13.80), and 8 of its 12 outlets pivot. So: Anker if the shopper wants outlet count for the money, Belkin if they want surge rating for the money. Both carry the full 1,875 W. A Dealectric TESSAN PS07 pick needs a warning that its 1,250 W cap (about 10.4 A at 120 V) is a third less than a standard 15 A strip. A space-heater-class load does not fit. Separately, Anker's own page lists TUV/FCC/ICES/CP65 and does not list UL. That matters because ChatGPT told the shopper to look for UL 1449.
